Pañcāṅga: "Five limbs" — the almanac of vāra, tithi, nakṣatra, yoga and karaṇa, all read from the Sun and Moon.
Vāra: The weekday. In the Tamil convention it changes at sunrise, not midnight, and is named for the planet ruling its first horā.
Tithi: A lunar day: each 12° the Moon gains on the Sun. Thirty tithis make one synodic month.
Pakṣa: A fortnight. Śukla (bright, waxing) runs to Pūrṇimā; Kṛṣṇa (dark, waning) runs to Amāvāsyā.
Śukla: The bright, waxing fortnight — tithis 1 to 15, ending at the full moon.
Kṛṣṇa: The dark, waning fortnight — tithis 16 to 30, ending at the new moon.
Pūrṇimā: Full moon: the 15th tithi, when the Moon is 168°–180° from the Sun.
Amāvāsyā: New moon: the 30th tithi, when the Moon closes the last 12° on the Sun.
Nakṣatra: A lunar mansion: one of 27 equal stretches of 13°20′ along the ecliptic. The Moon crosses one in about a day.
Pada: A quarter of a nakṣatra (3°20′). 27 × 4 = 108 padas circle the sky.
Yoga: The sum of the Sun's and Moon's longitudes, divided into 27 parts of 13°20′. Nine of the 27 are considered aśubha.
Karaṇa: Half a tithi (6° of elongation). 60 slots per month: seven movable names cycle eight times, plus four fixed ones.
Viṣṭi: Also called Bhadrā — the one movable karaṇa that is avoided for auspicious beginnings.
Aśubha: Inauspicious — traditionally avoided for new undertakings.
Nāḻigai: The Tamil ghaṭikā: 1/60 of a day, 24 minutes. The day is counted in nāḻigai from sunrise.
Muhūrta: Two nāḻigai (48 minutes); also an auspicious window chosen for an event. Always guidance, never a guarantee.
Abhijit: The 8th of the 15 daytime muhūrtas, around local noon — widely held auspicious.
Rāhu kālam: One eighth of daylight, chosen by weekday, traditionally avoided for beginnings.
Yamagaṇḍam: Another eighth of daylight by weekday, avoided for beginnings.
Kuḷikai: The eighth of daylight ruled by Gulika (Śani's son); work begun in it is said to repeat.
Horā: One of 24 planetary hours per day, lords in Chaldean order: Śani, Guru, Maṅgala, Sūrya, Śukra, Budha, Candra.
Rāśi: One of the 12 sidereal signs of 30°. The Sun's rāśi names the Tamil solar month.
Ayanāṁśa: The offset between the tropical and sidereal zodiacs (Lahiri: about 24°14′ in 2026), from the precession of the equinoxes.
Nirayana: Sidereal — longitudes measured from the fixed stars (Spica at 180°), not the moving equinox.
Elongation: E = λ☾ − λ☉: how far the Moon is ahead of the Sun. It sets both the tithi and the Moon's phase.
Ecliptic: The Sun's yearly path across the stars. The Moon is never more than about 5° from it.
Saṃvatsara: The year name in the 60-year Jovian cycle. The Tamil year begins in Chithirai.
Saṅkrānti: The moment the Sun enters a new rāśi — the start of a Tamil solar month.
Kṣaya: A tithi that begins and ends between two sunrises, so no day is named for it.
Adhika: A tithi that is in force at two successive sunrises, so two days share its name.
Candrāṣṭamam: Days when the Moon is in the 8th rāśi from one's birth rāśi; avoided for important work.
Graha: A 'seizer' — the visible planets, Sun and Moon, plus the lunar nodes Rāhu and Ketu.
